caption: Ashen knight at x3.2 half a second after stopping a walk: both boots planted wide on the turf; the lens sits behind its flank, the foreground is a dark shadow blob and the trees read blotchy.
Same stop 1.8 s later, after the settle steps and the release: the boots have not moved (the creep is gone); framing and lighting still not Wukong-grade.
Crown reel daze, front-lit: left gauntlet cupping the bowed helm, glaive drooped blade-first to the turf, knees buckled; armour reads dark and flat in the GL fallback renderer.

Crown reel impact frame, front-lit for the first time: the glaive is now knocked down across the body with the bowed head instead of standing at guard height; the giant's scale still does not read without the hero in frame.
The surge's coil from the knight's flank: down on its knee, hunched over the glaive as the plate cracks glow; a fallen slab darkens the foreground, and from the front the kneel barely reads.
The Ashen Knight's growth roar, front-lit at hour 9: glaive heaved up, fist raised, helm now thrown back; still small in frame at this distance and the knocked-down hero's pose is stiff.

Ashen Knight growth coil, front-lit: before (straight back, helm up) / after (spine curled, helm sunk between the shoulders) / flank after; the knight is still small in the lens and GL fallback lighting is flat.
The kneeling coil from the flank: back curled over the planted glaive, plate cracks glowing; the frame is wide and the boss small, not yet a Wukong shot.
Helm close-ups, crown-reel shake-off: old toss at 1.13 s (left, face level), new at 1.0 s (mid, still bowed) and 1.13 s (right, tossed back); low-res software render.
The Ashen Knight shaking off a plunge to the helm, front-lit: the helm now tosses back past level (+16 deg); the boss still reads small in this low lens.
Before: the slumped haft ran straight up the chest into the bowed helm's chin skirt (0.15 m/size through it) and the blade hung over the turf.

Ashen Knight's crown reel daze, front-lit: the glaive now angles out from the hip with its blade in the turf, clear of the bowed helm; the boss is still small in the lens and the helm's face never shows.
Crown hit-stop before (left: the glaive pointed at the lens at chest height, its blade edge-on across the throat) vs now (middle, rt 0.09; right, rt 0.14): blade already low and out to the side.
Ashen Knight crown reel, hit-stop frame front-lit at hour 9: the glaive is now knocked down with the head, blade toward the turf; the boss is still small in the lens and the armour reads dark.
Growth-surge heave, helm close-up, before (left) vs after (right): the glaive now rises beside the cracked helm instead of up through it; the GL fallback renderer still flattens the lighting.
Surge kneel from the flank, 2x crop, before (left) vs after (right): the haft's butt no longer rises through the bowed helm and the blade stays in the ash; the boss is still small in this lens.
Reveal opening, close lens: the haft now leans out beside the helm with the fist low on it (was running up under the helm); the cape texture is blotchy and the boss lacks fine surface detail.

Reveal opening, side lens: the dormant Ashen Knight leans on its planted glaive, haft now rising past the bowed helm instead of through it; the armour and cape still read flat and blotchy in the GL fallback.
Phase-2 surge wide: burning ring, knight heaving the glaive with the hero down in front; boss still only ~35% of frame height and backlit armour reads flat.

The hero knocked down by the Ashen Knight's growth blast, now stepped through its real knock-down in the surge shots: lying flat (st=50), back in guard (st=70); the hero is still tiny in this lens and GL lighting is flat.
New close surge lens: the Ashen Knight at its final phase-3 size fills the frame beside the 1.8 m hero; armour still reads flat dark red in the GL fallback renderer.
Close lens early in the growth surge (embers bursting from the helm seams, hero facing it); scale reads, but the knight's plate lacks metal sheen and the frame is GL-only.

The Ashen Knight now reads as fire-blackened steel with leather-bound legs and the oxblood surcoat as its only red (it was one flat dark-red figure); the legs are still near-black blobs with little detail.
Helm before (rust over half the plate), sparse rust only, and final: sparse rust plus a real steel reflectance, so the sun slides over the helm and pauldrons; the plate looks a touch too clean.
The phase-3 giant beside the hero with the new dark steel and leather; the plate now separates from the surcoat, but the GL fallback still lacks SDFGI/SSR and the boots are flat.
Ashen Knight full body in the reveal at 9:00: dark steel plate, red surcoat, strapped legs now show some banding; GL fallback lighting is still flat and the plate a touch clean.
Ashen Knight legs, before (left) vs now (right): the blackened leather straps' turns now read through rubbed brown lips with a dull sheen; the shaded leg is still very dark.

Ashen Knight helm before (top) and after (bottom): soot now runs down the blackened plate in vertical streaks with a few pale ash rivulets, breaking up the clean crown sheen; pauldrons still read clean.
Close reveal frame of the Ashen Knight with streaked plate; the surcoat still reads flat and the GL fallback renderer lacks GI.
Ashen Knight pauldrons before (top) and after (bottom): soot now packs the strip under each lame's rim so the worn-bright rims separate; still subtle, the GL fallback renderer lacks GI.
The Ashen Knight in the ring at hour 9 with sooted plate and pauldrons; legs in shade still read very dark and the scene lacks GI under the GL fallback.
Before this session: the same roar frame, where the head was flung back behind the gorget, so the giant seemed to have no head from the front.

The Ashen Knight's growth roar from the hero's low front view: the helm now stays over the collar with the visor tipped up and the glaive clear of it. Still wrong: the helm reads only as a dark crown with an ember rim, and the plate stays dark in GL.
Before this session: the same roar frame, the helm a dark crown with only sparks at its rim.

The Ashen Knight's growth roar from the knocked-down hero's view: the slit's fire now lights the tipped-up visor warm, so the helm reads as a face instead of a black crown; still wrong: GL renderer, the visor detail is soft at this range and the legs are very dark.

A Hollow Soldier 0.6 s after its walk swung 90 deg toward the lens: body square to its new line, mid-stride on a planted boot (the pace now carries round the corner instead of the walk snapping sideways); still GL fallback lighting, ring floor reads as flat dark dirt.
The x3.2 Ashen Knight mid-stride just after a 90 deg corner, on a planted boot with no skid; legs very dark in shade, GL renderer softness.
Ashen Knight's leg straps before (left) and after (right): the lit leather now has a warm brown sheen instead of a grey glaze; the shaded legs still read near-black (GL renderer).

Ashen Knight intro at 9:00: the shaded leather leg bindings now keep a brown fill so their turns read; still wrong: the plate legs in shade stay near-black and the GL fallback renderer softens everything.
Knight legs 2x crop, before (left) vs after (right): the shaded thigh straps go from a black blob to brown leather turns with dark creases; the shaded greaves are still black.

Hollow Soldier 10 frames after a walk stops, before (left) vs with the new chest sway (right): boots set clean in both; from this near-front lens the forward pitch barely reads, a side lens is still needed to judge it.

Ashen Knight x3.2 after a walk stops: before at f63 (left), with the chest sway at f63 (middle, helm carried forward) and f84 (right, rocked back); the sway reads but subtly, the bladed guard turns this lens 3/4-front, and the shaded leg plate is still near-black.

Hollow Soldier 6 frames after a walk stops, seen from the new side lens: the chest and hood carry on forward over the front boot, then rock back past upright by frame 72; the soldier still reads a little toy-like in hard sun and the bare ring floor is flat.
The x4.6 Ashen Knight striding away after a corner: boots planted and pace carried; the shin bindings read brown, but a bare grey ash knee still shows between the bindings.
The x4.6 knight settled after a stop, side lens: upright with boots planted; still reads small in frame and the knee gap shows grey.

Ashen Knight close-up at 9:00: the thigh straps in the surcoat's cast shadow now read as deep-brown leather turns instead of black blobs; the shins' ash body still reads flat grey and the plate is dark.
The x4.6 Ashen Knight stopping a walk, side lens: the helm carries forward over the front boot with the boots planted; the ring floor still reads flat and the legs dark.
Ashen Knight's knee, before (left: bare grey ash knee between the straps) and after (right: two short leather bindings close it); a small grey wedge still shows behind the bent knee.
x4.6 Ashen Knight striding in the ring with the knees bound; legs still read dark and flat from this backlit angle and the floor reads flat.
3x crop, before (left) vs after (right): the head now leans off the arm reaching overhead so the hat clears the fist; a subtle change, the reach itself still tops out at the brim.

Hero climbing the keep from behind mid-reach: the left fist rises beside the hat while the head tips away from it; still wrong: the right hand hides under the capelet, the hair reads as a grey blob and the fist peaks only just over the brim.
Climb from behind: the reaching right arm reads, but the low left hand is lost behind the mantle and bedroll; the wall's dark masonry and the warm hero read well.
Same frame with the mantle hidden (debug): the left arm is still invisible, so the mantle is not what hides it; the low hand is tucked in front of the chest behind the bedroll.

The hero climbing the keep from behind: the right fist reads up on its stone, the low left hand is still hidden behind the torso and bedroll (traced to the shoulders following the hip sway; no fix shipped yet), and the stone shows speckle noise in the GL fallback.
Side-on lens of the same climb from above: the reach to the stones reads, the figure is small and the low hand is lost behind the torso.
Hero climbing the keep's outer face, three-quarter from the left: hand-over-hand reads, but the hands hide under the hat brim and capelet and the bedroll fills the back.
Running jump at 0.3 s, before (left: legs hanging together) and after (right: push leg trailing, lead knee driven up). Still wrong: both arms held up in a boxer's guard, the hero lit dimly.
Running leap side-on at 0.12 / 0.30 / 0.50 s and 0.03 s into the landing: split stride, lead foot reaching, landing in stride. Still wrong: arms stiff, figure small and in shade.

Running leap side-on at 0.12/0.30/0.45 s: the arms now counter-swing (forward arm reaching ahead, back arm down past the hip) instead of a boxer's guard; the hero is still dim at this lens and the forward hand's fingers splay.
Full frame of the running leap at its rise: the pose reads as a leap, but the backlit hero, flat dark ground and empty yard would not pass as a Wukong shot.
Running leap side-on: the forward hand now closes into a loose half-fist instead of a splayed claw; the hero is still backlit and dim at this lens.
Leap forward hand before (left, fingers splayed and hooked) and after (right, curled into a loose fist); lighting on the hero still too dark.

Standing jump, before/after pairs (rise, apex): the near fist no longer sits up by the chin; arms reach forward and low with loose hands. Still backlit/dim at this lens and the drive frame passes a hand in front of the face.
Standing jump landing 0.06 s in: knees give, arms low and forward, no pop as the arm pose eases out. Lighting flat and the village behind is plain.

Standing jump from the side, old drive frame vs new at 0.10/0.13/0.20 s: the arms now swing up overhead nearly straight and then forward into the tuck instead of a forearm standing up by the face; still backlit and dim at this rear 3/4 lens.
Standing jump at 0.13 s: the near arm thrown up past the hat brim on the drive; the hero is still dark against the shaded cottage and seen from behind.
Standing jump drive (air 0.13 s), front lens with a key light: both arms now thrown up overhead in a V with the face clear; still the flat dirt test spot, and the hero reads small.
Standing jump front-lit: old drive (forearm across the face), new drive 0.10/0.13 s (hands overhead), and 0.20 s, where one hand still passes the mouth on the way into the tuck.
Standing jump at jt 0.20 after the fix: face and mask clear, far fist passes by the collar; ground still flat and the hero dim against a bright sky.
Standing jump, front-lit: old jt 0.20 (hand over the mouth) vs new 0.18 / 0.22 (arms come down from overhead in a wide arc, face clear); tuck arms still a little flat and wide.

Standing jump at the apex (front-lit): both forearms now gathered forward in front of the chest instead of held out wide in a T; still wrong: hands sit at chest height rather than down over the knees, the cottages read flat and the light is grey-dull.
Same tuck from the side: knees up, both hands reaching forward ahead of the knees; still wrong: the hero is backlit and dim against a pitch-black cottage wall.
Standing jump falling (jt 0.52, front-lit): both arms now open out to the sides at waist height for balance as the legs reach; the hero still reads dim and the yard is flat.

Old fall 0.44 / new 0.44 / new 0.52 / landing 0.05: the arms used to stay forward at chest height through the fall, now they open out and ease into the landing; hands could still rise a little higher.
Running leap from the front 3/4 (key light behind the lens): the forward fist now rides up in front of the chest; the face under the hat still reads dark and the back hand is lost behind the hip.

Running leap mid-flight from the rear 3/4: the forward arm now drives with the elbow bent and the forearm level instead of punched out straight; the hero is still small and dim in frame and the capelet hides the back arm.

Running leap mid-flight from a lit front 3/4: the forward fist now drives up to chin height with the forearm angled up like a sprinter's; the hero is still small in frame and the face under the hat reads dark.
Running leap frame strip (jt 0.12, 0.24, 0.36, landing): the forward arm arcs up from the hip to chin height and eases back down on landing with no pop; the back arm is still hidden behind the hip.
Plunge landing crouch at 0.15 s: knees deep, ferrule planted in the dust; the robe hides the legs' fold and the torso could fold further over the staff.

Plunge impact frame, side-on: the staff's ferrule now drives into the turf inside the earth burst with the fists down at chest height (before, it hung ~0.33 m over the ground); the chest still stays rather upright and the hero reads dim.

Plunge landing 0.15 s after impact, side-on: the chest now folds over the staff planted in the turf with the head lifted to look ahead under the brim; still wrong: the robe hides the knees' fold and the hero reads dim in the GL fallback.
Plunge landing 0.08 s, side-on: ferrule in the turf inside the earth burst as the chest starts to fold; still wrong: the burst's dust is flat-lit and the figure lacks rim light.

Running jump attack at jt 0.38, lit front 3/4: staff cocked back over the shoulder, but the front robe panel sticks straight out past the knee like a rigid red blade and the thigh wrap's open end shows at the knee.
Running jump attack at jt 0.48: the chest folds over the blow with the staff driven down ahead; the trunk has yawed so the lens sees the hero from behind, and the front panel still juts out stiff.
Old (left) vs new (right) at the same tick: the front panel (left strip) no longer runs on straight past the knee; the back panel (right strip) is unchanged and next to fix.

Running jump attack at jt 0.30: the front robe panel now folds at the knee and hangs plumb; still wrong: the back panel streams out behind as a rigid straight strip, the hero reads dim and is seen from behind mid-yaw.
Old (left) vs new (right) back panel in the running jump: the new tail bends down partway along instead of running out as one straight board; still too stiff and edge-on.
Running jump attack at 0.30 s: the back robe panel streaming behind now curls down under its own weight past mid-length; seen edge-on it still reads as a thin strip and the scene is dim GL.
Before (left, thin straight red strip) vs after (middle jt 0.38, right jt 0.32): the panel now twists open toward the hem; the hem tongues still read as straight spikes.

Running jump attack at jt 0.38 from the lit side: the back robe panel streaming behind now rolls to show its face and ragged hem; still a small figure in flat meadow light, legs' wrap ring at the knee open.
Before (left) vs after (right) at jt 0.38, 2x crop: the tongue tips drop a few cm toward the ground; from this edge-on lens the change is subtle.
Running jump attack at jt 0.32: the streaming back panel's torn hem tongues now hang down at their tips; still wrong: llvmpipe GL lighting, flat ground, tongues still read as thin strips.

Running jump attack, legs 4x: before (left) the foot binding ended in an open hollow pipe; after (right) every bandage wrap end rolls over and turns in to a small dimple. Still wrong: the foot wrap still reads as a tube over the boot, and the shin/thigh wraps are blunt cylinders at the knee.
Hero mid running jump attack from the side with the closed wrap cuffs. Still wrong: llvmpipe lighting is flat, the back robe panel's tongues are thin strips, the leg bindings look bulky.

Foot bindings before (left) vs now: the wraps narrow onto the ankle and over the instep, so the front boot toe comes out of a snug binding instead of a flared cuff; the rear foot still shows its dark sole end-on inside the ankle collar.
Running jump attack from the side with the tapered foot bindings; the legs still read as stacked cloth tubes and the GL fallback lighting is flat.
Hero's heels from a low rear lens, before (top) and after (bottom): the foot binding no longer stands round the boot heel as a wide pale cup; a flap still stands off the right ankle's buckle plate.
Idle hero's boots lit from behind: snug bindings over the ankle with bare leather heels; scene is dark under the hero's own shadow and the right ankle flap remains.
Low rear lens on the idle hero's heels after the side cap: bindings snug on the boot flanks, but the feet sit in the hero's own shadow and the ankle crescent remains.

Hero's right boot from behind, before (left) and after (right): the foot binding's outer-lower side no longer stands off the boot as a dark sheet from ankle to sole and the round buckle disc shows under it; a slim crescent still stands off at the ankle cuff.

Hero's near boot from the low rear heels lens, before (left) and with a tried tuck under the tapered binding (right): the dark crescent fin off the outer ankle is still there and the boot's vamp still covers the binding; the change was reverted.
Hero's feet from the front: left the old foot binding with a dark sheet off each boot's flank, right the binding removed so the boot shows bare; the boot leather is still too pale and soft-looking.
Hero's heels from behind with no foot binding: buckle disc and heel show, shin wrap ends at the ankle; pale leather reads a little like a sneaker.

Hero's boots before (left: pale grey leather with a red heel, like a sneaker) and after (right: dark worn brown leather, oxblood heel, no grazing sheen), from behind and front; a grey strap by the ankle buckle still shows.
Front 3/4 at ankle height: the boots now read as worn oiled brown leather under the shin bindings; the boots still lack stitching/sole detail up close.

Hero's near boot from behind, before (left) and after (right): the pale blue-grey strap under the ankle buckle was the leather's white sheen on a dark band; it now reads as dark brown leather. Still wrong: the boots have no stitching or sole detail up close.
Low lens behind the idle hero: both boots read as worn brown leather with a dark strap and buckle disc; the scene around is still flat turf and the light is dim at the feet.
Soldier's feet from the front 3/4: slimmer foot bindings over the instep; the plated toes still read as cracked white ceramic, not worn iron.
Hollow soldier's feet from behind, before (left) and after (right): the foot binding no longer stands off the outer ankle as a dark flap and hugs the heel; the sabaton is still a too-clean pale grey.

Hollow soldier's feet from behind, before (left: pale grey sabatons with drawn-on cracks, like ceramic) and after (right: blackened worn iron with a dull sheen); the iron is still a fairly even blue-grey, rust barely shows.
Front 3/4 at shin height: both sabatons and the ankle buckle now read as dark iron under the bindings; the bindings' wood-grain-like banding and the flat grey iron still look less than Wukong-grade.
Heel counter from behind, before (left) and after (right): darker iron with a browner lower edge and a kept metal sheen; the change is modest and the plate still looks too smooth.

Hollow soldier's sabatons front-on after the wear pass: the iron now reads near-black with a sheen on the toe instead of pale grey; rust and mud at the sole still hardly show in this light, and the hemp bindings' banding still reads like wood grain.

Hollow soldier's shin binding front-on, before (left: even plank-like turns with fine grain lines and a seam down the middle) and after (right: uneven strips of different tone, grime blotches across the turns, no seam); the lap creases are still very regular.
Low front lens on a Hollow soldier's legs: the shin bindings now read as dirty, unevenly wound hemp strips rather than wood; the sabatons below are still too smooth and the ground texture is flat.

Running jump attack at the cock (jt 0.30), before | after: the pelvis and belt now point along the flight with the lead knee driving ahead, instead of bladed 43 deg off it; still a small, dark rear-3/4 GL frame.

Running jump attack at the fold (jt 0.48), before | after: hips and belt square across the body instead of turned away; this lens still sees the hero from behind and the figure is too small to sell the blow.
Standing jump attack coming down toward the lens: hips square to the strike; the foreshortened staff reads as a vertical line over the face from this lens and the GL lighting is flat.

Standing jump attack at the cock, front 3/4 (left before, right now): the belt and sash now run square across the hips with the knees driving at the lens instead of the pelvis bladed off the blow; still a modest change, and the figure stays dark and small in the GL fallback renderer.
Standing jump attack at jt 0.55 with the squarer hips: knees drive at the lens under a centred robe panel; the staff over the face still reads as a thin vertical line.

Standing jump attack front-on at jt 0.45/0.55: left the old 0.3 hip share, middle/right the new 0.6 share with the belt square across the body and the robe panel hanging centred between the knees; still wrong: the staff comes down as a foreshortened vertical line over the face from this lens.
Hero from behind at idle: the glider roll now sits snug across the sash with the staff tucked past it; grass and lighting hold up, the cottage behind is still flat and dark.

Running jump attack at the blow from a front 3/4: the furled glider roll now stays on the sash against the back instead of floating beside the shoulder; the hero still reads small in the frame and the turf is flat and dark.
Standing jump attack at jt 0.53 front-on with the new key: hands come down in front of the chest with the shaft clear of the face; hips square, robe centred.

Standing jump attack at jt 0.55 front-on, before (left) and after the canted pass: the shaft now runs beside the right cheek instead of over the nose, but from dead front it still reads as a near-vertical line.
Before (19:30 key, JA_CANT_PREV=1) at jt 0.55 for comparison: the shaft stands vertical just off the nose.

Standing jump attack front-on at jt 0.53 with the new canted key: the shaft now comes down as a diagonal over the hero's right shoulder instead of a vertical line up the face; it still crosses the right eye and brim edge.
Same move at jt 0.55: hands at chest height, shaft canted up to the hero's right; the hat brim still sits behind the shaft and the figure is dark in the GL fallback.

Standing jump attack front-on at jt 0.55 with the new head roll: the head tips away from the canted shaft so the whole face reads beside it. The shaft still crosses the hat brim and the figure is dark in the GL fallback.
Before (JA_SWING_TILT=0), same frame: the shaft crosses straight over the right eye.
Standing jump attack at jt 0.55 with the stronger head roll: the face is clear of the canted shaft. The figure still reads dark under the GL fallback.

Jump attack front-on, close-ups: 0.35 rad head roll at jt 0.53 (left), the new 0.5 rad roll at jt 0.53 (middle) and at jt 0.55 (right). The shaft moves a little further off the cheek, but at 0.53 it still touches the mask's edge.
Standing jump attack at jt 0.55 with the faster tilt fade: face clear of the canted shaft; the figure still reads dark under the GL fallback.

Jump attack front-on close-ups: old tilt fade at jt 0.53 (left), the new earlier fade at jt 0.53 (middle), and the new fade at jt 0.51 (right). At 0.53 the shaft clears the cheek a little more; at 0.51 the vertical shaft still crosses the mask's edge.

Jump attack front-on at jt 0.585 (u ~0.51), before (left) and with the new pass key (right): the fists now stay on the hero's right and the shaft sweeps under the chin instead of rising to the mask; the swing reads a touch flatter there.
Standing jump attack mid-downswing with the pass key: face clear, staff diagonal across the chest; still wrong: a stray light shaft hangs in the air at left, the figure is dark in the GL fallback.

Standing jump attack front-on at jt 0.585, before (left) and after (right): the swing trail no longer stands in the air as a ruled, striped light shaft, it is a faint soft smear; still wrong: the figure is dark in the GL fallback and the blow reads a little flat.
Jump attack from behind at jt 0.55: the trail off the staff tip is a soft pale smear instead of a hard band; still wrong: the hero reads dark and small against a flat midday field.
Standing jump attack front-on at jt 0.565: current pass key (left) vs a tried chop key (right) that stands the shaft upright beside the face; rejected as a stalled blow. Figure still dark in GL.
Standing jump attack from behind at jt 0.565/0.585/0.605: the canted downswing reads as a chop toward the foe; the front-on 'flat' bar is the forward strike's projection. Still dark, hands small.
Rear 3/4 of the idle hero: the sheathed staff now lies over the furled glider roll at the sash instead of running through it; figure still dark in the GL renderer.
Running from the follow camera: the staff, now also tied at the hip, keeps its line down the left leg with no tail behind the hero; lighting dim, small in frame.
Hero's madder robe in the jump attack, before (left: moth holes read as black specks) and after (right: clean cloth, torn hem kept); the pale knee caps still read as grey plastic blocks.
Standing jump attack front-on at jt 0.585 with the hole-free robe; figure still dark in GL, pale knee caps and a sky sun-shaft streak remain.
Knee caps before (left, pale grey plastic) and after (right, dark leather in line with the shin wraps), 2x crop of the same frame.
Standing jump attack front-on: the knee caps are now dark worn leather guards instead of pale grey blocks; the figure is still dark in GL and the sky's sun-shaft streak remains.

Soldier's leg bindings from behind in shade, before (left: wavy contour rings from shadow acne) and after (clean wound strips); the sabatons still read grey and the foreground stone reads as a soft block.
Hero and Hollow soldier squaring up in the meadow at 11:00 with the fixed bindings; figures still cast shadows, but the faces/hood and the house read flat and dark.
